findings.title: Reschedule flow cancels old EMAIL reminders immediately via SendGrid, reintroducing the exact limit bug this PR fixes
findings.body: When rescheduling a booking, the old booking's EMAIL workflow reminders are cancelled with `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` — the `immediateDelete=true` flag causes an immediate SendGrid 'cancel' API call. According to the PR description, calling this SendGrid endpoint immediately is exactly what caused the original bug: SendGrid only allows up to 100 pending cancellations, and once that limit is hit, new cancellations fail silently and reminder emails keep being sent. The fix elsewhere (handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx `requestReschedule`) correctly avoids this by calling `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without the immediate flag, deferring the actual SendGrid cancellation to the new CRON job that only cancels within the last hour before send. This reschedule code path is the one explicitly named in the PR title ('...and rescheduled bookings...') yet still uses the broken immediate-cancel strategy, so under moderate reschedule volume the same SendGrid pending-cancellation limit can be hit again and reminder emails for rescheduled bookings can still be sent.

findings.title: A single failed SendGrid cancellation aborts cancellation of all other reminders in the same cron run
findings.body: The new cancellation loop wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop (including the SendGrid `client.request` call for every reminder and the final `Promise.all`) in one try/catch. If the SendGrid cancel request throws for one reminder (e.g. transient network error, stale/invalid batch id), the loop stops immediately and none of the remaining reminders in that batch get their cancellation request sent during this cron invocation, nor are their WorkflowReminder rows deleted. Because the cron only runs every 15 minutes and only reminders due within the next hour are considered, a persistently-failing single entry can repeatedly block processing of the rest of the batch on every subsequent run (since the same failing item is encountered again before reaching later items), risking that otherwise-cancellable reminders are still sent by SendGrid because the cancel call never reaches them in time. Cancellation and deletion should be handled per-item with its own try/catch so one failure doesn't block the others.

findings.title: Immediate cancellation path never deletes or updates the WorkflowReminder DB row
findings.body: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, when `immediateDelete` is true, the function calls SendGrid to cancel the scheduled send and then simply `return`s — it never deletes the WorkflowReminder row nor sets `cancelled: true`. This leaves a stale row in the database that still looks 'scheduled' (scheduled=true, cancelled=null/false) even though the underlying email was cancelled. The row only gets cleaned up later by the unrelated generic cleanup in scheduleEmailReminders.ts (`deleteMany` where `scheduledDate <= now`), once its original scheduledDate passes, potentially leaving inconsistent/stale state in the table for a long time and making this data unreliable for any other logic or UI that inspects WorkflowReminder rows in the meantime.

findings.title: Old booking's workflow reminders are cancelled before confirming the reschedule actually succeeded
findings.body: The cancellation of `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` happens unconditionally right before calling `eventManager.reschedule(...)`, regardless of whether that reschedule call later succeeds. Further down, the code explicitly checks `if (results.length > 0 && results.some((res) => !res.success))` and merely logs an error without rolling back — the booking's calendar/video integrations may fail, but the original booking's reminders have already been cancelled irreversibly (for EMAIL, moved to immediate-SendGrid-cancel / for SMS, outright deleted from Twilio and the DB). This can leave a booking that effectively did not get successfully rescheduled with no reminders scheduled at all.

findings.title: Defense-in-depth ownership check dropped from WorkflowReminder cancel/delete mutations
findings.body: Previously (e.g. in workflows.tsx update mutation) the WorkflowReminder deletion query included an ownership guard directly in the Prisma `where` clause (`booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }`), so even if an upstream bug allowed another user's reminder id to reach this code, the mutation itself would affect 0 rows. The new shared helpers `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (used from multiple callers including trpc routers) perform `update`/`delete` solely by `id`, with no ownership check baked into the query. This removes a layer of protection against reminder ids leaking across callers/users and now relies entirely on each caller's upstream query having correctly scoped the reminder list.

findings.title: Generic past-due cleanup can delete a cancelled reminder before its SendGrid cancellation request is ever sent
findings.body: The handler first runs an unconditional cleanup: `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { method: EMAIL, scheduledDate: { lte: now } } })`, deleting any EMAIL reminder whose scheduledDate has passed, regardless of its `cancelled` flag. This runs before the new cancellation block that queries `cancelled: true` reminders due within the next hour. Because the cron runs every 15 minutes, if a reminder is marked `cancelled: true` less than one cron interval before its `scheduledDate`, the next cron execution may find `scheduledDate <= now` already true by the time it runs and delete the row in the first cleanup step — without ever having issued the SendGrid 'cancel' request for it. If SendGrid had not yet actually sent the email at that instant, it will still go out as originally scheduled, since it was never told to cancel. This narrow but real race window undermines the PR's goal for reminders cancelled close to their send time.

findings.title: No automated tests for the new cancellation logic despite history of a broken prior fix
findings.body: The PR description states that the previous fix (PR #6991) for this exact issue 'was wrong and didn't work as expected.' This PR introduces new, non-trivial logic (the `cancelled` flag lifecycle across emailReminderManager.ts, smsReminderManager.ts, and the new cron cancellation block in scheduleEmailReminders.ts) that is central to actually fixing the reported bug, yet no unit/integration tests are added to verify that cancelled/rescheduled bookings' scheduled reminders are correctly prevented from sending. Given the history of this exact feature being silently broken in production, the lack of test coverage is a significant risk for a repeat regression.
